Vs

full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam J : At the instance of the petitioner, Anis Ahmed, and auction  purchaser this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the Order No. 29 dated 25-10-2003 passed by the Court of 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka setting aside the Auction Sale dated 17-11-2001 in Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2002 arising out of Money Execution Case No. 60 of 2000 (Annexure-A) should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 2. The background leading to the Rule, in short, is that the writ petitioner who is an auction purchaser challenges the legality of the order No. 29 dated 25-10-2003 passed by the 4th Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as Adalat) allowing the application under Order XXI rule 90 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to set aside the auction sale arising out of Money Execution Case No. 60 of 2000. 

 4. The respondent No. 5 and 6 did not contest the suit and the suit was decreed ex parte. The decree holder bank thereafter filed Money Execution Case No. 60 of 2000 on 15-11-2000 for realization of the decreetal amount against the judgment debtor. In compliance of the Code of Civil Procedure the execution case proceeded wherein auction notice was issued on 17-12-2001. Three bidders participated in the bid and eventually the bid submitted by the petitioner was considered to be the highest and accepted thereby confirming the sale by the Adalat on 17-1-2002. 

 5. The petitioner was utterly shocked and surprised to learn thereafter that on 7-4-2002 the Respondent Nos. 2, one Masud Ahmed and 3 Mrs Nurun Nahar Dolly being applicants filed Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 2002 before the Adalat challenging the said auction sale Order XXI rule 90 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the grounds that the scheduled property was purchased in the joint name of the respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 5; that no notice was served upon the respondent No. 2, 3 and 5 and that there was material irregularities in the auction proceedings. Be it mentioned that in the said Miscellaneous Case the bank and the present petitioner auction  purchaser was made opposite party No. 3 and 4 respectively. The petitioner filed written objection (Annexure-F) and the Adalat on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case by his order dated 25-10-2003 allowed the Miscellaneous Case by setting aside the auction sale. Against which the petitioner, the auction purchaser moved this Division and obtained the present Rule and stay. 

 6. Mr Rafique-ul Huq, the Senior Advocate appearing with Masood R Sobhan and Mr Omar Sadat, the learned Advocates for the petitioner after placing the petition and the relevant Annexure with it argued that the order impugned against is without lawful authority and without any legal effect on different counts. He mainly contended that in passing the impugned order the Court below travelled beyond the ambit or order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure and set aside the auction sale allowing the Miscellaneous Case. In elaborating his contentions, the learned senior Advocate has assailed the impugned order from various angle and pointed how the Adalat acted wrongly in setting aside the same. 

 7. Mr KM Zabir with Mr AKM Enayed Hossain, the learned Counsels appearing for the respondent Nos. 2, 3, 5 and 6 by filing affidavit-in-opposition on the other hand, opposes the Rule. The respondent No. 4 Rupali Bank Limited also entered appearance by filing Vokalatnama in the case. The bone of contention of the respondents is that this Writ Petition is not maintainable in its present form. It has been argued that the impugned order is an appealable order and the petitioner can well ventilate his grievance by bringing an appeal before the proper forum. 

 9. But the learned Counsel for the respondents on the other hand has raised the preliminary point on the question of maintainability of this Writ Petition. Mr Zabir submits that the impugned order is an appealable order and such Writ Petition is not maintainable. Substantiating his argument the learned Counsel further submits that decision  in a Miscellaneous Case under Order XXI Rule  90 is appealable as per the Code of Civil  Procedure. Further he submits that the order impugned against cannot be challenged under the writ certiorari since under this jurisdiction this Court will be loath to give its decision as a Court of appeal. Mainly on these counts the learned Counsel for the respondents submits that in all fairness this Rule should be discharged outright. 

 10. The contention of the learned Counsel for the respondents holds good. Firstly, we hold that a application under Article 102 of the constitution against any order passed under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure is misconceived. Secondly in writ certiorari this Court certainly would be loath to interfere with a decision of the Court below as a Court of appeal. This proposition of law is well settled and consistently observed by the Appellate Division as well as this Division.
